First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta =2{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{4x}{3}$, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡(\frac{4x}{3})=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{8x}{3})+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3/2}({cosh}^{2}⁡(\frac{4x}{3})+7x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}(\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{8x}{3})+1)+7x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{8x}{3})+\frac{1}{2}+7x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3}{16}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\frac{8x}{3})+\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2})|}_{0}^{3/2} \\  & =[\frac{3}{16}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\frac{8\cdot (3/2)}{3})+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}+\frac{7}{2}{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}]-[\frac{3}{16}\operatorname{sinh}⁡0+0+\frac{7}{2}\cdot {0}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{3}{16}\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡(4)+\frac{69}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
